newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends sharply down, storm ignores crop.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends sharply down, storm ignores crop.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled sharply weaker after Tropical Storm Josephine failed to live up to expectations and devastate crops throughout the Southeast, industry sources said.
"This was a classic case of 'buy the rumor, sell the fact'," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes.
Floor sources blamed today's losses on local and trade selling and a dearth of buying until the December contract hit 75.50, where trade fixation buying provided support.
The December contract closed 1.80 weaker at 75.85, having ranged from 77.45 to 75.50. The deferred contracts finished 1.73 to 0.70 lower.
While today's market fell on the lack of damage to the crop, it would have also fallen if the storm had hurt crops, since weaker output would buoy imports and cut exports, Ganes noted.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its latest supply and demand data Friday at 0830 EDT.
"People didn't want to stay long the market going into the crop report," Ganes said.
